swimlanes.label: Facilitator Mode
swimlanes.description: Phases 1-4 from PHASED_IMPL: visible connections, critique, timing, signal control.

swimlanes.label: Autonomous Facilitator
swimlanes.description: Phase 6 local-only automation after Facilitator Mode is stable.

swimlanes.label: UX Polish Driver
swimlanes.description: Current sprint: visual hierarchy, motion, timing, signal control, micro-interactions, critique tone, and final demo consistency.

swimlanes.label: Collaborative Sync
swimlanes.description: BroadcastChannel, Yjs, WebRTC, and peer-aware synchronization backlog.

swimlanes.label: Integrations
swimlanes.description: Local-doc search, declarative WebMCP, and external system writeback backlog.

swimlanes.label: Architecture
swimlanes.description: Board-first domain, patch-journal state, beat runtime, and WebMCP boundary work required to align the app with the integration guide.

swimlanes.label: Design Implementation
swimlanes.description: Inline companion, beat review UX, undo/history, layout cutover, and guide-fidelity interaction work.

meta.scratchpad: bo-029, bo-030, and bo-031 are landed in code. The next priority is browser proof for bo-009 two-tab Yjs sync, followed by bo-013 File System Access permission-loss and re-authorization validation. After those truth-seeking checks, the next design slice is bo-032 beat review flow.

tasks.title: Phase 1: Canvas connection overlay foundation
tasks.goal: Render existing Connection records directly on the canvas as a bounded SVG overlay so relationships are visible without opening the drawer.
tasks.comment: Claiming Phase 1 foundation work.
definition_of_done: Canvas renders up to 8-10 high-signal connections with style by kind.
Connected line endpoints update while an attached idea is being dragged.
Clicking a connection line highlights both endpoint ideas without breaking drag, group, or merge flows.
constraints: Reuse existing Connection records; do not introduce a new persisted connection model.
Keep the overlay non-intrusive and preserve current canvas interactions.

context.notes: Canvas now renders a bounded SVG connection overlay with drag-aware endpoints and click-to-highlight behavior.

tasks.title: Phase 1: Add draw_connection WebMCP tool
tasks.goal: Expose a WebMCP tool that creates a visible connection between two ideas in one call and routes through the same app state used by the canvas overlay.
tasks.comment: Keep this tool aligned with the existing dispatch-and-wait tool path; agents should be able to narrate and render the link in one action.
definition_of_done: A global draw_connection tool is registered and documented alongside find_connections.
Calling the tool results in a visible connection on the canvas.
Tool output clearly reports what was connected and how it was classified.
constraints: Do not add hidden coupling between the tool and future critique/timing systems.
Preserve the existing StrictMode-safe registration pattern.

context.notes: draw_connection is registered as a global WebMCP tool and threads through app-owned board connection state.

tasks.title: Phase 2: Persisted critique system
tasks.goal: Add the critique storage, WebMCP tools, and anchored critique-card UI so the app can challenge ideas sharply without interrupting flow.
tasks.comment: There is already a devilsAdvocate role in the phase pipeline, but this phase requires a separate persisted critique system with its own store, tools, and card UI.
definition_of_done: Critiques persist in a dedicated store and survive reloads.
critique_idea, list_critiques, and dismiss_critique are exposed through WebMCP.
Critique cards anchor near the target idea and never block interaction.
constraints: Critiques must appear only after idle and must not spam the board.
Critique phrasing should be sharp and specific rather than generic.

context.notes: Persisted critiques now have a dedicated IDB store, anchored canvas cards, and critique/list/dismiss WebMCP tools.

tasks.title: Phase 3: Soft mode inference timing layer
tasks.goal: Infer whether the board is exploring, structuring, stressing, or converging, then time AI actions subtly without adding explicit mode toggles.
tasks.comment: This phase should control timing, not decision authority. The UI cue must be subtle and fade if ignored.
definition_of_done: A lightweight inferredMode classifier exists with a reason and confidence.
Mode output drives the appropriate non-blocking suggestion or tool trigger path.
No mode toggle is added to the UI.
constraints: Never interrupt typing or dragging.
Only act after idle and never force a mode switch.

context.notes: Starting the timing layer after syncing completed facilitator slices.

tasks.title: Phase 4: Signal control and noise reduction
tasks.goal: Bound critiques, suggestions, and connections so the system stays trustworthy as more autonomous behavior lands.
tasks.comment: Do not scale broken signal. Thresholding and cooldowns should come after the underlying connection and critique signals are correct.
definition_of_done: Connection confidence threshold is enforced.
Per-idea critique cooldown prevents spam.
Suggestion deduplication and visible-count bounds keep the canvas clean.
constraints: Maximum 2 critiques per idea, 6 visible suggestions, and 10 connections total.
Keep all control logic aligned with the existing live board state.

tasks.title: Phase 5: Turn-log pagination
tasks.goal: Split large turn-log payloads out of get_idea so debugging and agent inspection scale without oversized responses.
tasks.comment: This is the observability sidecar the roadmap calls out for future connectionFinder and devilsAdvocate turn-log growth.
definition_of_done: get_turn_log returns paginated entries with nextCursor.
get_idea returns turn-log summary metadata instead of the full array.
Agent-side inspection can retrieve history incrementally.
constraints: Do not lose existing turn-log data.
Keep the new tool shape consistent with current WebMCP tool conventions.

tasks.title: Phase 6: Local autonomous facilitator
tasks.goal: Add bounded observer-driven automation so the system can add value without explicit user commands and without overwhelming the user.
tasks.comment: This remains local-only and should not start until the earlier facilitator phases are stable.
definition_of_done: State-change observers trigger bounded tool actions under explicit safeguards.
A global pause toggle exists.
AI-originated actions are tagged so the user can distinguish them from direct edits.
constraints: No sync or Yjs work starts here.
Human interruptibility must remain immediate.

tasks.title: Phase 7: Demo polish
tasks.goal: Refine animation timing, transitions, and layout so the facilitator behaviors read as intentional and impressive during the demo.
tasks.comment: This closes the sequence only after the earlier functional phases are working and stable.
definition_of_done: Connection, critique, and suggestion moments animate smoothly.
UI transitions avoid abrupt jumps.
The board reads as polished on desktop and mobile.
constraints: Do not hide unresolved functional issues with polish work.
Preserve the existing visual language rather than replacing it.

tasks.title: 4.1 Two-tab BroadcastChannel + Yjs sync spike
tasks.goal: Prove zero-server two-tab sync by wrapping the ideas store in a Y.Map with BroadcastChannel transport and y-indexeddb persistence.
tasks.comment: The Yjs plus BroadcastChannel plus y-indexeddb idea-store spike is landed in code; the remaining work is live two-tab browser proof and concurrent merge validation before the full CRDT port.
definition_of_done: Adding an idea in tab A appears in tab B in under 100ms on the same machine.
The ideas store is backed by a Y.Map with BroadcastChannel transport.
Reload preserves shared state through y-indexeddb while docs, suggestions, and groups stay IDB-only.
constraints: Do not start full-store Yjs migration in this slice.
Keep the spike isolated to the ideas store and validate concurrent panel-drag merge behavior.

context.notes: Implementation is in branch truth; the remaining proof step is browser validation before bo-010.

tasks.title: 4.2 Full CRDT port for board stores
tasks.goal: Replace direct IDB writes across board stores with Y.Doc-backed mutations and ship a one-shot migration path from existing local data.
tasks.comment: Yjs is a storage rewrite, not a feature flag, so the port layer must hide the backend from UI and tool code.
definition_of_done: Storage helpers route through Y.Doc-backed mutations across the board stores.
First boot after upgrade migrates existing IDB data into the Y.Doc once.
UI and WebMCP tools operate unchanged through the storage port layer.
constraints: Do not keep a parallel IDB plus Yjs write path.
Migration must preserve existing board data and avoid two sources of truth.

context.notes: This follows the two-tab spike and should stay behind a clean storage port.

tasks.title: 4.3 WebRTC cross-machine sync with SDP-only broker
tasks.goal: Extend collaborative sync across machines by swapping BroadcastChannel transport for y-webrtc and adding the minimal SDP-broker room flow.
tasks.comment: The broker may pass SDP offers only; it must never carry Y.Doc payload.
definition_of_done: Peers can join a room across machines using a short room code or invite URL.
Remote sync uses y-webrtc instead of BroadcastChannel.
The signaling path carries SDP offers only and keeps idea payloads peer-to-peer.
constraints: Do not ship manual token-paste signaling.
Keep the broker minimal and avoid central storage of board contents.

context.notes: The roadmap explicitly rejects manual token-paste signaling even as a stopgap.

tasks.title: 4.4 CRDT-driven autonomous facilitator triggers
tasks.goal: Move facilitator triggers onto Y.Doc update events with idle gating, AI-host election, and AI-origin dedup so exactly one peer automates the board.
tasks.comment: This is the multi-peer follow-on to the current local-only facilitator and must stay human-interruptible.
definition_of_done: The observer subscribes to Y.Doc update events rather than local-only board state.
Exactly one peer claims AI-host responsibility via awareness-based election.
AI-originated transactions are tagged and deduped across peers.
constraints: Preserve global pause and bounded automation behavior.
Avoid duplicate ghost panels or repeated role runs during split-brain or host handoff.

context.notes: Peer-aware automation starts only after sync is real.

tasks.title: Stretch: search_local_docs local RAG tool
tasks.goal: Let the user grant a local docs folder and search PRDs/specs with File System Access-backed local retrieval surfaced as supporting-doc candidates or scout context.
tasks.comment: Local doc search and the re-authorize flow are landed in code; the remaining work is browser validation of File System Access permission loss and recovery.
definition_of_done: A user can grant a folder and issue local doc searches from the app.
Matches surface as supporting-doc candidates or scout context rather than opaque raw snippets.
The app has a deliberate re-authorize flow for per-session permission loss.
constraints: Do not hide the File System Access permission boundary.
Do not assume persistent folder grants across reloads.

context.notes: Implementation is present, but the permission UX still needs live browser proof before this should be treated as done.

tasks.title: Stretch: cross_pollinate role and tool
tasks.goal: Introduce a dedicated cross_pollinate role that finds two distinct ideas and proposes a third merged concept with clearer intent than scout_ideas.
tasks.comment: This is partially covered by scout_ideas today, but splitting the role would sharpen synthesis-specific prompting and UI.
definition_of_done: A dedicated cross_pollinate role exists with structured output.
A WebMCP tool exposes the role on the standalone board surface.
The resulting suggestion clearly attributes the two source ideas it combines.
constraints: Do not duplicate scout_ideas behavior without a sharper synthesis contract.
Keep the output anchored to existing ideas rather than free-floating unrelated suggestions.

context.notes: This is a dedicated synthesis verb beyond the current scout behavior.

tasks.title: Stretch: declarative WebMCP + toolautosubmit
tasks.goal: Add agent-aware declarative form fields that emit tool calls on change when Chrome preview support is good enough.
tasks.comment: This remains blocked on Chrome preview validation, so it should stay behind the sync backlog.
definition_of_done: Declarative form fields can emit tool calls on change for supported surfaces.
The implementation is validated against the Chrome preview requirements called out in the WebMCP docs.
Unsupported environments degrade cleanly without breaking existing manual tools.
constraints: Do not ship this before preview validation is real.
Keep HTTP and manual tool invocation paths working without declarative support.

context.notes: Roadmap explicitly marks this as blocked on Chrome 146 preview validation.

tasks.title: Stretch: multi-user facilitator UX
tasks.goal: Once sync is real, add speaker tracking, consensus summaries, and end-of-session action-item capture that make facilitator behavior legible in collaborative sessions.
tasks.comment: This belongs after sync and peer-aware automation are stable enough to trust in shared sessions.
definition_of_done: Collaborative sessions surface facilitator-owned consensus summaries and action items.
The UX is designed for multi-user sessions rather than single-user board nudges.
The feature reads as an extension of the shared facilitator rather than a separate tool silo.
constraints: Do not start before sync and peer-aware facilitator plumbing are stable.
Keep the facilitator non-intrusive even in active discussions.

context.notes: This is explicitly downstream of the collaborative sync track.

tasks.title: Stretch: W1 external system integration tools
tasks.goal: Use the W1 active-tab tool path to let phase transitions write to Linear, Jira, or PRD tools with explicit second-step consent.
tasks.comment: This should extend the existing W1 consume path rather than invent a separate integration channel.
definition_of_done: The app can chain active-tab tool writes into supported external systems.
Phase-transition writeback requires an explicit second consent step.
The integration reuses existing W1 patterns instead of introducing a parallel bridge.
constraints: Do not bypass explicit consent for external writes.
Preserve the existing active-tab consumption architecture.

context.notes: This is the explicit W1 writeback stretch item from the roadmap.

tasks.title: 3.1 Visual hierarchy pass
tasks.goal: Make the current canvas instantly legible by establishing one active focus, stronger structure weighting, critique dominance, and slight de-emphasis of irrelevant ideas.
tasks.comment: Start with hierarchy before animation so the board has a stable visual grammar.
definition_of_done: Exactly one idea can read as active at a time through subtle elevation and accent treatment.
Strongest connections render with the clearest weight while secondary structure fades to roughly 60-70% opacity.
Critique cards visually outrank structure without covering or blocking their target ideas.
constraints: Do not add new UI surfaces or persistent clutter.
Maintain readability on dense boards and keep non-active ideas above readability thresholds.

context.notes: The board should tell the user what matters before any new motion layer is added.

tasks.title: 3.2 Motion design and reveal animation
tasks.goal: Make connections, critiques, suggestions, and highlight feedback animate with directional, idle-gated motion that feels intentional rather than abrupt.
tasks.comment: Directional motion should explain what just happened without becoming theatrical.
definition_of_done: Connections draw from source to target over roughly 300-500ms with stroke-dash animation.
Critiques enter with a 10-20px offset and 200-300ms fade-slide after idle.
Suggestions and connection-click highlights follow the same motion language and timing band.
constraints: Never animate during drag or typing.
Support reduced-motion fallbacks without losing state clarity.

context.notes: Motion needs to read as explanation, not decoration.

tasks.title: 3.3 Sequential idle-gated facilitator timing
tasks.goal: Resequence facilitator output so the board reveals one structural insight, then one critique, then later a suggestion only after a stable idle window.
tasks.comment: The magic layer is sequencing, cancellation, and patience rather than more output.
definition_of_done: Idle detection waits roughly 1.2-2.0 seconds after the last interaction before showing anything.
Queued AI actions reveal one at a time with 600-1000ms spacing in the order connection, critique, suggestion.
Any user interaction cancels pending AI reveals and resets timing cleanly.
constraints: Do not allow simultaneous insight reveals.
Do not interrupt typing, drag, dismiss, or edit flows.

context.notes: This is the patience layer that prevents the facilitator from feeling noisy or random.

tasks.title: 3.4 Signal control and overflow refinement
tasks.goal: Keep the facilitator trustworthy by enforcing hard visible limits, hiding weak signals, and collapsing overflow without adding new panels.
tasks.comment: Do not scale broken signal; show fewer, stronger insights and degrade overflow gracefully.
definition_of_done: Visible output stays within the roadmap bounds for connections, critiques per idea, and suggestions.
Weak connections are filtered out entirely while secondary but valid signals de-emphasize smoothly.
Suggestion overflow collapses into an existing-surface '+N more' affordance rather than a new panel.
constraints: Apply limits without making data disappear abruptly.
Use confidence and rank ordering rather than FIFO truncation.

context.notes: The board should stay clean even when the facilitator has more candidate output.

tasks.title: 3.5 Micro-interactions and board responsiveness
tasks.goal: Add subtle drag, hover, edit, and grouping reactions that make the current board feel aware and alive without increasing noise.
tasks.comment: These reactions should reward attention and preserve calm, not create constant motion.
definition_of_done: Nearby connections react smoothly during drag with light elastic tension instead of rigid snapping.
Critiques soften during edits and regain full presence after idle returns.
Hovering an idea highlights related connections and critiques as one coherent set.
constraints: Avoid jitter under high-frequency drag updates.
Do not let hover or edit feedback fight the idle-gated reveal queue.

context.notes: Responsiveness matters, but the board still has to feel calm and deliberate.

tasks.title: 3.6 Critique tone and language tightening
tasks.goal: Reshape critique output so every card sounds like a sharp collaborator using brief, direct challenge language instead of generic summaries.
tasks.comment: The critique voice should increase trust by being concise, pointed, and obviously actionable.
definition_of_done: Critiques bias toward direct formulations such as 'This fails if...' and 'You're assuming...'.
Each critique fits within 2-3 short lines without long passive summary paragraphs.
Persisted and regenerated critiques both respect the same terse copy standard.
constraints: Do not let prompt shaping regress critique specificity.
Do not exceed the existing card footprint.

context.notes: Sharper language is part of perceived intelligence, not just copy polish.

tasks.title: 3.7 Final consistency and demo-quality polish
tasks.goal: Unify spacing, easing, durations, and color discipline across the existing facilitator surfaces so the whole experience reads as one intentional system.
tasks.comment: This closes the polish driver only after hierarchy, motion, timing, and tone are already aligned.
definition_of_done: Connection, critique, and suggestion surfaces share the same 200-500ms timing band and ease-out motion language.
Spacing and alignment feel consistent across desktop and narrow viewport layouts.
Color discipline stays strict: critique in red/orange, structure in blue/grey, suggestions in teal.
constraints: Do not paper over unresolved interaction bugs with visual polish.
Keep the current product shape rather than redesigning it.

context.notes: The close-out pass should make the demo feel smooth, deliberate, and premium.

tasks.title: Design Core: board document and board-scoped repositories
tasks.goal: Replace the web app's phase-first hot path with a canonical board document and board-scoped stores for boards, ideas, connections, critiques, turns, and tweaks, with a migration bridge from existing local data.
tasks.comment: Starting board-first domain and board-scoped repository cutover from the Integration Guide target state.
definition_of_done: A canonical Board document or aggregate exists and the web app reads board-scoped state from it.
IndexedDB stores cover boards, ideas, connections, critiques, turns, and tweaks through one hydration path.
Legacy phase fields are isolated behind an adapter so the board path stops depending on Idea.phase in the hot path.
constraints: Do not keep two durable sources of truth for the same board entities.
Migration must preserve existing local board data and current web app startup behavior.

context.notes: Completed the board-first repository cutover for the standalone web app: App now hydrates from a board repository snapshot, workspace phase rendering is isolated behind a legacy adapter, and WebMCP lifecycle tools consume a legacy tool projection instead of the raw selected board idea.

tasks.title: Design Core: patch journal and reversible BoardController
tasks.goal: Route all committed board mutations through a central BoardController that emits forward and inverse JSON patches, persists ChangeSets, and becomes the only mutation path for user and AI actions.
tasks.comment: Completed the live journal cutover: committed board mutations across the web app, WebMCP tools, workspace shell, sidepanel consent/create flows, and fallback forms now route through the boardController changeSet path, with dead compatibility writes removed from the board repository. Verification: npm run typecheck passes; vite builds remain blocked by local ENOSPC on dist outputs.
definition_of_done: All committed board mutations route through a single applyChange or equivalent mutation API.
ChangeSets persist forward and inverse JSON patches with actor, summary, and affected entity metadata.
Undo and redo replay the journal rather than rebuilding state ad hoc from UI handlers.
constraints: Human and AI changes must share the same journal semantics.
Ephemeral beat drafts must stay separate from committed board state until the user keeps them or automation is explicitly allowed.

context.notes: This is the mechanism behind undo/redo, change history, and reversible AI structural edits.

tasks.title: Design Core: beat runtime and proposal contract
tasks.goal: Replace the current web-app phase loop with a board-level callBeat runtime for scout, connect, critique, cluster, and summarise, using strict JSON beat outputs and candidate proposals instead of direct structural writes.
tasks.comment: Completed the beat runtime/proposal contract slice. Added `src/beats/types.ts`, `src/orchestrator/beatRegistry.ts`, `src/orchestrator/runBeat.ts`, and `apps/web/beatContext.ts`; introduced the `boardSummariser` role; routed the live scout/connect/critique paths in `apps/web/App.tsx` through typed beat envelopes before commit; surfaced active beat state in the header; and tightened `ChangeActor.beat` typing. Verification: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:web`, and `npm run build` all pass.
definition_of_done: The web path exposes exactly five beats: scout, connect, critique, cluster, and summarise.
Each beat returns strict JSON with candidates, sources, confidence metadata, and patch payloads or equivalent change intents.
Automatic and manual beat triggers are encoded with visible state for small versus big beats.
constraints: Do not let freeform AI responses mutate board structure directly.
Retain narrow role prompts and machine-parseable outputs for every beat.

context.notes: This is the contract shift from phase progression to board beats.

tasks.title: Design Core: board-first WebMCP surface
tasks.goal: Retarget the existing WebMCP boundary around board verbs and beat runs instead of legacy phase and workspace concepts, while keeping the direct web app WebMCP integration.
tasks.comment: Completed the board-first WebMCP surface cut. Added `get_board` and `run_beat` to `apps/web/webmcp-tools.ts`, wired `brainstorm:runBeat` handling in `apps/web/App.tsx`, and demoted the legacy phase-local WebMCP lifecycle registrations so the active surface is board-first and beat-first. Verification: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:web`, and `npm run build` all pass.
definition_of_done: Board tools cover the board document, beat invocation, candidate admission or dismissal, and connection or critique operations through the board controller.
dispatch-and-wait or equivalent request handling stays intact for the standalone web app.
Tool handlers operate on current board and beat-run state rather than phase-local state.
constraints: Keep the direct WebMCP surface; do not add a second UI abstraction layer such as a2ui.
Do not duplicate orchestration logic across App state and tool handlers.

context.notes: This preserves WebMCP while aligning it to the guide's board and beat model.

tasks.title: Design Core: extract board shell from apps/web/App.tsx
tasks.goal: Break the monolithic App.tsx into board controller, storage sync, beat orchestration, and inspector modules so board-first behavior is testable and the workspace drawer stops owning the hot path.
tasks.comment: Landed in code: App.tsx is down to the board shell and layout while session actions, analysis actions, suggestion actions, sync, companion automation, and WebMCP event bridges all live behind explicit hooks.
definition_of_done: App.tsx no longer owns history mutation logic, storage choreography, facilitator timing, and layout concerns in one file.
Board controller and board UI hooks have explicit boundaries and callers.
Workspace surfaces remain available as secondary inspector or export views rather than primary orchestration surfaces.
constraints: Preserve current app boot, tool registration, and board interaction behavior while extracting modules.
Do not strand dead code paths behind the old workspace-first model.

context.notes: Build-verified on branch truth; the board shell extraction is landed and downstream work should treat bo-029 as complete.

tasks.title: Design Core: durable turns, tweaks, tombstones, and reversible deletes
tasks.goal: Complete the persistence layer for beat runs, turn history, tweak state, and tombstones so dismissed AI outputs remain reversible and history-backed instead of being hard-deleted or left in transient component state.
tasks.comment: Landed in code: settings now persist through IndexedDB-backed storage, beat runs are durable, and reversible artifact handling uses board-scoped persistence instead of web-only chrome.storage semantics.
definition_of_done: Turns, beat runs, tweak state, and tombstones persist in board-scoped storage.
Dismissed or deleted AI artifacts are represented as reversible tombstones rather than silent hard deletes.
Web settings or tweak persistence no longer depend on chrome.storage.local for the web path without a compatible abstraction.
constraints: Do not lose existing local settings or board data during the storage move.
History data must stay compatible with undo and redo semantics from the patch journal.

context.notes: Build-verified on branch truth; downstream work should treat the durable storage move as landed.

tasks.title: Design UI: always-on Dev companion and idle-triggered beats
tasks.goal: Make the Dev companion visibly present while the user edits the board, with automatic idle-triggered runs, explicit watching or drafting states, and visible beat activity when something big is happening or the user asks for it.
tasks.comment: Landed in code: the board now has an always-on companion surface with idle-gated automation, visible state, and beat-progress affordances.
definition_of_done: The board shows companion presence and state while the user is editing or when beats are running.
Automatic beat triggering is idle-gated and tied to meaningful board changes.
Big beats can reveal active beat progress and interim idea or source discovery state without forcing it on every small edit.
constraints: Do not interrupt active editing or hijack focus while the user is typing or dragging.
Preserve human interruptibility and global pause behavior.

context.notes: Build-verified on branch truth; the remaining follow-up is refinement, not initial implementation.

tasks.title: Design UI: beat review flow with keep or scratch candidates
tasks.goal: Surface big-beat outputs as reviewable candidate ideas, sources, connections, critiques, and structural edits that the user can keep or scratch individually or as a group before they become committed board changes.
tasks.comment: This is the core human-in-the-loop layer for AI structural changes.
definition_of_done: Beat review UI shows candidate items with provenance, summaries, and the affected ideas or structures.
Keep commits the candidate into the board journal; scratch creates a tombstone and preserves the decision in history.
Users can accept a subset of a beat without discarding the rest of the run.
constraints: Do not auto-commit structural AI edits without an explicit keep path or a narrowly defined low-risk automation rule.
Dismissed items must remain recoverable through history rather than disappearing silently.

context.notes: Matches the requested keep or scratch flow for beats and candidate ideas.

tasks.title: Design UI: undo or redo controls and change history timeline
tasks.goal: Add visible undo and redo controls plus a readable change history that groups user and AI changes by actor, beat, and patch set so the board can move backward and forward safely.
tasks.comment: The patch journal only matters if the user can actually navigate it from the board UI.
definition_of_done: Undo and redo controls are visible and operate across user and AI-authored changes.
A history surface shows actor, beat, summary, timestamp, and affected board entities for each ChangeSet.
Moving backward and forward preserves board consistency and does not drop persisted state.
constraints: Do not fall back to snapshot-only history that loses semantic change information.
Guard against replaying inverse patches against the wrong board revision.

context.notes: Implements the user-visible history and navigation controls requested for patch-backed state.

tasks.title: Design UI: board-first layout cutover and inline AI surfaces
tasks.goal: Make the canvas the primary product surface, move workspace detail into a secondary inspector role, and replace the remaining workspace-first interaction path with inline board-native AI affordances.
tasks.comment: The current right-side workspace slideover still carries too much of the product interaction model.
definition_of_done: Primary brainstorm flow happens on the board with inline AI artifacts and review surfaces.
Workspace or drawer surfaces are secondary inspectors, not the place where the main loop lives.
No sidebar-chat style surface becomes the primary AI interaction model.
constraints: Preserve desktop and mobile usability while moving controls onto the board.
Do not regress current board interactions such as drag, grouping, or selection.

context.notes: Delivers the board-first cutover called for by the guide.

tasks.title: Design UI: cluster and summarise beats
tasks.goal: Implement the missing cluster and summarise beats with inline group proposals, board-level thematic labeling, and summaries that stay connected to board entities and beat history.
tasks.comment: The guide defines five beats; the current app still behaves like connect, critique, scout plus helper logic.
definition_of_done: Cluster beat can propose grouping or regrouping operations with user review.
Summarise beat produces board-level digests tied back to ideas, sources, or groups.
Both beats show up in beat history and use the same proposal and keep or scratch contract as the rest of the system.
constraints: Do not ship cluster or summary behavior as ad hoc side effects outside the beat runtime.
Summaries must reference real board entities rather than floating free text alone.

context.notes: Closes the missing beat gap between the current app and the target interaction model.

tasks.title: Design UI: source-linked metadata edits and structural idea operations
tasks.goal: Let kept beat candidates append metadata to existing ideas, attach sources, create entirely new ideas, rewrite idea structure, or modify existing relationships while preserving provenance and reversibility.
tasks.comment: Accepted beat output must be able to enrich existing ideas, not only create detached suggestion cards.
definition_of_done: Accepted candidates can create new ideas, enrich existing idea metadata, attach sources, or modify structure through the board controller.
Every structural edit retains provenance and remains reversible through the patch journal.
The board can represent changed idea structure without losing the prior state or source linkage.
constraints: Do not treat source attachment or structure edits as opaque text blobs.
All structural AI edits must be attributable and reversible.

context.notes: Implements the user's requirement that kept beats can enrich, create, or restructure board ideas.

tasks.title: Design UI: final integration-guide fidelity and accessibility pass
tasks.goal: Align the shipped experience with the guide's intended visual language, reveal choreography, accessibility, theme behavior, and empty or loading states once the board-first interaction model is in place.
tasks.comment: This is the final fit-and-finish pass after the architecture and interaction model are in place.
definition_of_done: Theme and motion behavior align with the guide across sketch and whiteboard modes.
Keyboard, focus, and screen-reader behaviors cover the new inline AI and history surfaces.
Empty, loading, thinking, kept, and scratched states feel intentional rather than bolted on.
constraints: Do not trade away board responsiveness for decorative polish.
Avoid generic assistant UI patterns that conflict with the design guide's visual direction.

context.notes: Final guide-alignment pass after the board-first interaction model lands.
